headline: Another child dies as measles cases hit 84,266 in Bangladesh
summary: The DGHS reports 126 new cases in 24 hours, with Dhaka Division recording the highest number of deaths from the highly infectious disease.
details: Another child with measles symptoms has died in Bangladesh, with 126 new cases reported in the last 24 hours according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Since March 15, a total of 92 people have died from confirmed infections, while another 551 people have died showing symptoms of the disease.
The Dhaka Division has been the hardest hit, recording 232 deaths among those with suspected measles, followed by 86 deaths in the Rajshahi Division.
In the past 24 hours alone, 1,027 people with symptoms sought treatment, and 878 were admitted to hospitals.
Dhaka saw the highest number of admissions with 309 cases, while Rangpur recorded the lowest with 16 admissions.
Overall, the total number of suspected measles cases in the country has reached 84,266, with 10,185 cases officially confirmed.

headline_marked: 19,346 runs and 48 centuries: [[Kane Williamson retires from international cricket]]
headline: 19,346 runs and 48 centuries: Kane Williamson retires from international cricket
summary: The former New Zealand captain ends a stellar 16-year career as the country's highest run-scorer across all formats.
details: New Zealand cricket legend Kane Williamson has announced his retirement from international cricket, bringing a curtain down on a magnificent 16-year career.
As New Zealand's highest run-scorer in international cricket, Williamson amassed 19,346 runs across three formats, including 48 centuries and 6 double centuries.
Between 2016 and 2024, he led the Black Caps to two ICC World Cup finals and secured the ICC World Test Championship title in 2021.
Williamson stated that he had been thinking about retirement for some time and felt that now was the right moment to step away while still possessing a strong drive for the game.
He expressed pride in having given his absolute best in every match for New Zealand and felt fortunate to leave the game on his own terms.
His individual accolades include being named the ICC Cricketer of the Year in 2015 and the ICC Test Player of the Year in 2019, along with four Sir Richard Hadlee Medals.
Due to the sudden announcement, Williamson will not participate in the remainder of the ongoing Test series against England.
New Zealand has not yet announced who will be called up to the squad to replace the legendary batsman.
caption:
The end of an era for the Black Caps. 🏏

Kane Williamson retires with 19,346 international runs.

New Zealand cricket legend Kane Williamson has announced his retirement from international cricket, bringing a curtain down on a magnificent 16-year career.

As New Zealand's highest run-scorer in international cricket, Williamson amassed 19,346 runs across three formats, including 48 centuries and 6 double centuries.

Between 2016 and 2024, he led the Black Caps to two ICC World Cup finals and secured the ICC World Test Championship title in 2021.

Williamson stated that he had been thinking about retirement for some time and felt that now was the right moment to step away while still possessing a strong drive for the game.

He expressed pride in having given his absolute best in every match for New Zealand and felt fortunate to leave the game on his own terms.

His individual accolades include being named the ICC Cricketer of the Year in 2015 and the ICC Test Player of the Year in 2019, along with four Sir Richard Hadlee Medals.

Due to the sudden announcement, Williamson will not participate in the remainder of the ongoing Test series against England.

New Zealand has not yet announced who will be called up to the squad to replace the legendary batsman.
